CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  February 8, 2021 - 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 2:04 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Rivas.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVID-19 in Pasadena, the nation, and around the world.

SPECIAL ITEM  COVID-19 UPDATE FROM DR. YING-YING GOH, PUBLIC
  HEALTH OFFICER

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided introductory comments, and
  Dr. Ying-Ying Goh, Public Health Officer, provided an update on
  COVID-19 positive cases, including the number of cases where
  people gather (work, socially or otherwise), amended thresholds for
Councilmember Hampton  opening schools, information on COVID-19 vaccines provided to
connected to the meeting at
  adults 65 years and older, as well as first responders, and Public
2:13 p.m.
  Health Department's outreach in administering the COVID-19
  vaccines; and responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson thanked Dr. Goh and her staff for their work
  administering the COVID-19 vaccine to the senior community and
  first responders .

  Councilmember Hampton thanked Dr. Goh for her work in assisting
  the schools that have opened for in-class learning; and advocated
  for the City to issue a statement regarding the recent Supreme
  Court ruling to eliminate the state's prohibition on indoor worship.

Council Minutes  1  02/08/2021
   Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the City issuing
  any statement on the Supreme Court ruling stating he believes the
  reaction by the state and the City's Health Director were
  appropriate. He spoke on the need to meet with Pasadena Unified
  School District (PUSD) Board to discuss the reopening of public
  schools and a mandatory vaccination policy for staff and students.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, responded that the annual joint meeting
  of the PUSD Board of Education and the City Council is scheduled
  for Monday, March 1, 2021.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the importance of recognizing how much
  families and kids are struggling with remote learning, and the
  increasing need and demand for a return to in-class instruction and
  extracurricular activities. He asked staff to develop a "basic tool kit"
  to distribute to the schools to help them prepare for the re-opening
  and return of in-person learning at Pasadena schools.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that a number of letters and emails
  advocating for the reopening of schools in Pasadena, were
  received, which were distributed to the City Council, posted on-line,
  and made part of the public record from the following individuals:

  Erika Foy, representing Save California Students Now
  Gary Stern, representing Pasadena Area School Heads
  (PASH)
  Tonya Beilstein, Jon Bracker, Julia Fanara, Sister Carolyn
  McCormack, Elizabeth McGregor, Kate Morin, Amy Patzlaff,
  Gary Stern, and Baudelia Taylor, Heal of School (for various
  schools)

  In addition, Latasha Reese, Assistant City Clerk, together with the
  City Clerk, read aloud comments advocating for the reopening of
  schools in Pasadena, and providing comments/suggestions from
  the following individuals:

  Mary Forrest, Pasadena resident
  Marisa Zakaria, Pasadena resident
  Harper Burge, Pasadena resident
  Caroline Botsford, Pasadena resident
  Nicole Anido, Pasadena resident
  Catherine Roheim, Pasadena resident
  Brian Botsford, Pasadena resident
  Marissa Bell, Pasadena resident
  Melissa K. Eaves, Pasadena resident

  Henry Burge, Pasadena resident
  Frances Morrison, Pasadena resident
  Ryan Forrest, Pasadena resident

Council Minutes  2  02/08/2021
   Greg Chapman, Pasadena resident
  Hayley Boaz, Pasadena resident
  Alyson Pernecky, Pasadena resident
  Dana Banta, Pasadena resident
  Denise Walklett, Pasadena resident
  Celene Lyddon, Pasadena resident
  Diana Sala, Pasadena resident
  Angela Buchanan, Pasadena resident
  Noelle Aloe, San Marino resident
  Toi Treister, Pasadena resident
  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident

  Mayor Gordo asked staff to include on his upcoming Joint Mayors
  Meeting agenda (with Mayor Garcetti of Los Angeles and Mayor
  Garcia of the City of Long Beach) the topic of reopening and
  returning to in-class instruction as a discussion topic for the meeting
  scheduled for Wednesday, February 10, 2021. He spoke on the
  need for staff to distinguish the issue related to the City being tied
  to Los Angeles County in terms of COVID-19 case numbers.

  Councilmember Williams stated that at some point the City will need
  to have a discussion to determine if it is necessary to continue on
  the same path and follow the State of California regulations, or to
  consider a separate path and develop specific health and safety
  guidelines for the City of Pasadena as it relates to COVID-19.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke on the mental health risks and
  educational impacts of remote learning for school age students, and
  asked Dr. Goh to advise the City Council when she feels the costs
  of remote learning exceeds the health benefits gained in adhering
  to COVID-19 safety protocols.

  The City Council recessed at 3:30 pm., and reconvened at 4:01 p.m.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for the reopening of in-class
  instruction for all grade levels; and spoke in favor of pushing back
  on California regulations related to the reopening of in-class
  instruction, stating that the mental health impacts to the children are
  of grave concern.

  Councilmember Williams stated that she believes there is a
  structural problem with the Emergency Orders, which she believes
  has eviscerated decision-making authority and power of the City
  Council, and spoke in favor of amending the Emergency Orders to
  allow public policy decisions to return to the City Council.

  Michele Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor, clarified that the
  State Legislature, through adopted statutes, provided the Governor
  with the authority to enact statewide emergency orders, and the City
  may develop orders more restrictive but not less restrictive.

Council Minutes  3  02/08/2021
   Councilmember Madison stated that he strongly supports
  complying with state legislation and the legally issued emergency
  declarations of the Governor.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT  NO.  30469,  PLANNED
  DEVELOPMENT  NO.  34,  100  WEST  WALNUT
  (LINCOLN/PARSONS PROJECT, PROJECT PROPERTY
  LOCATED AT 10 WEST WALNUT AVENUE)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed amendments to the Development
  Agreement do not involve physical changes to the environment and,
  if adopted, are therefore exempt from the requirements of CEQA
  pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3);
  (2) Direct the City Manager to negotiate amendments to the
  Development Agreement pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code
  (PMC) 17.66.0BO(A) consistent with the topics identified in the
  agenda report; and
  (3) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an amended Development
  Agreement within 60 days for City Council consideration of the
  terms to which the parties agree at a subsequent meeting . (Contract
  No. 30469-1)

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, opened the public hearing; reported that
  the public hearing notice was published in the Pasadena Press on
  January 21, 2021 ; and that a number of letters and emails providing
  comments/suggestions related to local hiring and contracting, which
  were distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and made part
  of the public record were received from the following individuals:

  Rick Olsen, representing Letner Roofing Co.
  Cliff Smith, representing United Union of  Roofers,
  Waterproofers, and Allied Workers
  Sanfilippo Construction
  Logan Shea, residence not stated
  Gor Grishyan, representing Giniani Corporation
  Adam Preciado, representing Tineo Sheet Metal

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, David
  Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and responded
  to questions.

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns with the dismal results of the
  project developer in complying with provisions contained in the
  Development Agreement related to local hire and procurement.

Council Minutes  6  02/08/2021
   Vice Mayor Wilson stated the following for the record, "As a result
  of outreach from the applicant and one of their representatives, I
  had a conversation with them about this project just to get some
  information. This occurred before I was on the Council, so I just
  want the record to reflect that."

  Rob Kane, representing Lincoln Property West, provided an oral
  overview of the local hire and procurement efforts made by Lincoln
  Property West (Lincoln/Parsons Project, Project Property Located
  At 10 West Walnut Avenue) and the various community benefits
  these efforts have resulted for Pasadena residents and businesses,
  including fees paid for transportation, utilities, and permits, fees
  paid towards affordable housing and infrastructure improvements,
  funds spent to purchase local materials and supplies, and
  commitment to public accessibility to open space. He provided
  information on their outreach for their local hire program; and
  responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky read aloud comments, concerns, support, and

Council Minutes  7  02/08/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy requested the following for the record:
  "Mr. Kane for the record, from your perspective in the terms of the
  20%, 20% and 15% what is the dollar number if you had in fact
  reached what we are calling "goals" under those three categories?"

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's question, Mr. Kane
  responded by saying that over the next 60 days the development
  team will work closely and collaboratively with the City to develop a
  strategy to address those numbers.

  Mr. Kennedy also requested the following for the record, "So, my
  rough on the napkin arithmetic would lead me to believe that the
  total benefit in terms of a dollar amount is about $70 million if we
  had been successful on this project. And $70 million is significantly
  more than the approximate $20 million that has been floated earlier
  today and is in the staff report, Mr. Kane. So I just want to put that
  on the record. It is not hard and fast, and I've asked you to give me
  your number so we would all be on the same page as it relates to
  what is spent on hiring, contracting and local sourcing of materials."

  Councilmember Hampton expressed concerns with the lack of fiscal
  data in the staff report and from the developer related to 20% of the
  project budget that would have been spent on local hire and
  procurement; and spoke on the Pasadena City College training
  program where students were shown the project site, but not hired
  to work on the project.

  In response to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry related to the
  City's assistance to the developer with local hiring, City Manager
  Mermell reported that City staff, the City's First Source Program,
  and additional contractual staff (Mr. Prentice Deadrick) have been
  working with the developer to help meet their local hire and
  procurement goals.

  Councilmember Rivas spoke on the need to seek reimbursement
  from the developer for any City costs incurred associated with hiring
  additional staff to provide assistance to the developer to meet their
  local hire and procurement goals.

  Mayor Gordo recommended that staff be directed to negotiate with
  the developer on a Community Benefit Agreement or Project Labor
  Agreement that will allow the developer to have access to pre-
  apprenticeship and apprenticeship programs (i.e. Flintridge Center)
  as a way to support the achievement of the Development
  Agreement contract goals; and spoke in favor of seeking
  reimbursement of the costs incurred by the City associated with
  providing assistance to the developer.

  Councilmember Masuda and Williams spoke in favor of staff
  negotiating with the developer.

Council Minutes  8  02/08/2021
   Councilmembers Hampton and Kennedy spoke in favor of holding
  the developer accountable in Phases I and II of the "Lincoln Project"
  as the developer agreed to the percentages related to local hire and
  procurement detailed in the Development Agreement No. 30469.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested that the direction to staff as
  part of the Development Agreement amendment, negotiate
  reimbursement of expenses incurred by the City; ensure staff "true-
  ups" the percentages related to local hire, contracting, and sourcing
  procurement without excuse (with the developer willing to divide
  major contracts to reach the negotiated numbers that the City
  Council approves); and renegotiate the Development Agreement
  for the current phase of the project, and not only Phase II of the
  project. He spoke on the necessity of the developer to further
  commit to local contracting and local sourcing efforts.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke in favor of directing staff to amend
  Development Agreement No. 30469 to look for alternative
  opportunities for the developer to provide community benefits and
  capture value in a different method.

  Mayor Gordo requested staff return to the City Council with an
  amended Development Agreement proposal that addresses both
  the contribution to the City's expenses, as well as provides real
  opportunities for pre-apprenticeship and apprenticeship programs.
  He requested that staff work with the developer to provide a
  breakdown of the 112 positions hired by the developer and the
  number of hours worked at each position related to the project.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Kennedy,
  seconded by Vice Mayor Wilson, to close the public hearing:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor
  Gordo
  NOES:  None
